course_description: This course focuses on arts linked to the African continent as well as operations of museums. It examines how objects enter museum collections and what information accompanies objects when they arrive at museums. The course does not require previous study of Africa, African arts, or museums.
course_notes: (Same as ARTHIST 282 1) In Claiming Space! An Intro to African Arts, Architecture, and Museums, we will carefully look at and think about objects and spaces linked to the African continent as well as museums that house African arts. During the first part of the semester, we will focus on case studies connected to present-day Senegal. During the second part of the semester, we will consider case studies connected to present-day Ghana. Together we will identify broader themes that emerge through the case studies and may be relevant for the study of arts, architecture, and museums elsewhere on the continent and across its diasporas. Our study of older and newer arts will lead us to ask probing questions, identify reliable sources, and evaluate available evidence. We will develop informed insights about certain objects and sites; the specific people who shaped and experienced them; and the histories that arts, architecture, and museums engage. We will reflect on what the term African can signify in different contexts. We will also consider practicalities and ethics related to the movement and display in European and North American museums of older and newer objects created by artists linked to the African continent. And we will think broadly about what it means for us and for anyone else, whether from now or another time, to be human and to embrace our shared humanity. Art History major/minor: Division III or IV Art History with Museums Concentration: core or elective Architectural Studies minor: elective
